content.body:
The Bristol Blenheim was designed as a fast twin-engine intruder, but by 1940 its impressive speed had been eclipsed handily by even the medium and heavy bomber designs of the day, to say nothing of the fast pursuit fighters like the 109. Redeployed as an anti-shipping attack aircraft, the Blenheim series eventually spawned the Beaufighter design, which was the more true expression and functionally better airframe. However, the Blenheim served well if not heroically during the opening of WWII in a multitude of roles.
The Mk IV was the pure bomber of the series. With its complex bombsight, bombardiers could hit targets accurately if the flight profile was very stable. But this left the lightly-armed intruder very vulnerable. As a result, it was only marginally effective as a level bomber. Far more suited to fast low level attacks, the Blenheim was fitted with additional external bomb loads and used to far better effect in support and anti-shipping roles.
Blenheim squadrons suffered terrible losses in 1940 as the principal attack bomber flying against the well-protected ports where shipping was being assembled for Operation Sealion, the planned German invasion of Britain.
Stay as fast as you can in the Mk IV and do not engage enemy fighters under any circumstances. A low level approach followed by a 'pop up' to safe drop altitude when nearing the target will help to keep you undetected. Drop your bombs and get out of the target area as fast as you can, because without your bomb load you are an intruder with no weapons and completely vulnerable.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Pilot 2 Bombardier 3 Top Gunner
